Drive Alert supports speed-limit compliance and safer driving. Camera data comes mainly from OpenStreetMap volunteers (open data) and may be incomplete, outdated or wrong. Drive Alert collects precise location data to warn you about traffic cameras ahead. While the app is open it shows your position on the map. After you press Start Drive, location is also used when Drive Alert is closed or not in use, for example while Google Maps is on screen or the phone is locked, until the drive ends. Drive Alert treats your location as sensitive personal data. It reads your location only while you use the app or while camera alerts you started are running, processes it on your phone, and never sells it or uses it for advertising. Your position itself leaves the phone only in a camera report you explicitly choose to publish; the map does load map images for the area around you from OpenFreeMap (see Server communication).

While Drive Alert is open, it reads your current location on the phone to show where you are on the map, list nearby cameras with their distance and direction from you, check GPS accuracy, and attach a position to a camera report you are writing. When you press Start Drive, it uses precise location until you stop alerts, the drive ends, or 30 minutes pass without movement, including while other apps such as Google Maps are on screen and while the phone is locked; a notification is shown the whole time. When the app is closed and alerts are off, Drive Alert does not use your location.

Camera matching happens on the phone using the downloaded camera database. Alert history (which camera was announced and when, without your coordinates) and your settings are stored only on the phone and are excluded from cloud backup.

Over encrypted HTTPS only. Camera data: about once a day (and when you tap Update now) Drive Alert downloads the public OpenStreetMap camera file from GitHub; the file itself is refreshed weekly and the request contains no location or trip data. Map: the map opens around your position and loads map images for the area shown from OpenFreeMap, which (like any website) can see your IP address and that area. Alerts work without the map and fully offline.

Reports stay on your phone unless you tick “Publish publicly on OpenStreetMap”. Then the report text and one position are published as a public OpenStreetMap note without an account name: your phone’s current position for new, temporary and wrong-position reports, or the mapped camera’s position for other reports. Anyone can read notes. OpenStreetMap receives your IP address and stores it with the note (visible to its administrators). Published notes cannot be deleted from the app.

Drive Alert does not upload trip history, does not sell location data or share it with advertisers, does not show ads, does not read your Google Maps route or other apps’ screens, and does not log precise coordinates in production builds.
Alert history older than 30 days is deleted automatically. You can delete all local history at any time in Settings.
You can stop alerts at any time, revoke location or notification permission in Android settings, delete local history, or uninstall the app to remove all data stored on the phone.

Drive Alert is an open-source project. For privacy questions, data requests or grievances, open an issue at github.com/Ansh1040/map/issues (do not post personal data there; ask for a private contact instead).
